figures.title: This paper in the 13 components, against the field
figures.subtitle: Each box: what this paper does, then common practice across all sensors and how many ledger papers share it.
figures.caption: Verdicts compare the paper's choice for each component with common practice across 8,995 ledger entries on any sensor (silent speech, brain-to-text, lip reading), not only lip-reading papers. Paper counts come from the maintainer's ledger and undercount some components, notably language models, confirmation and correction.

M01.note: Inherited from the LRW data pipeline.

M02.note: Automatic labels as in LRW; slot under-recorded in the ledger.

M03.note: No earlier example in the wiki (recall estimate 0.78), but the gain (76.5 to 61.1% WER) is one run on one dataset and not separated from sub-sequence augmentation, so not ahead.

M06.field: Attention seq2seq decoding from non-audio signals
M06.note: No earlier example in the wiki (all pre-2017-05 hits read; topic recall estimate 0.33); results on LRS, LRW and GRID, but LRW/GRID fine-tune the LRS model, so method and data scale are not separated; not ahead.

M07.note: Common practice; the M07 slot itself is under-recorded.

M11.field: In-the-wild sentence test sets; speaker-disjoint only in some
M11.note: Train/test speaker overlap not reported; the authors only say thousands of speakers make the model speaker agnostic.

choice: CER, WER, unigram BLEU; one run
M12.field: Machine vs human lipreader on the same material
M12.note: Whether the 50.2% was scored on the same 200 clips, and run-to-run variance, are not reported.

choice: Release promised in arXiv v2 only; never released
